title: The Editors’ Table
paragraphs: At a table covered with draft pages, a group of young editors discussed their next publication. Each person had brought a different account. Rather than rank the experiences from best to worst, they decided to explore the connections among them and preserve the details that mattered.

The opening pages introduced several situations worth examining carefully. The conservator examined the statue's mutilation. The captain feared a mutiny among the angry crew. The exhibition offered myriad examples of inventive design. The defeat marked the nadir of the team's season.

The remaining pages widened the discussion with additional observations. The announcement launched a nationwide campaign. The old record gave the place of his nativity. The biology diagram illustrated an area of necrosis. His negativism made every discussion difficult.

By the end of the discussion, the students had learned why careful reading requires more than a quick judgment. A useful interpretation must fit the details of the situation. They chose a conclusion that acknowledged differences among the accounts, and they left readers with a question: which observation most strongly supports your view, and what might change your mind?
